item.title: Laudatory Speech for Professor Michael Weber on Receiving the Alexander von Humboldt Professorship | Keynote-Rede ESMT Berlin

rating.summary: This speech is a laudatory address delivered at ESMT Berlin honoring Professor Michael Weber on receiving the Alexander von Humboldt Professorship. The speaker, Fritzi Köhler-Geib of the Bundesbank, highlights Weber's academic contributions in monetary economics, heterogeneity, and expectation formation, as well as his collaboration with the Bundesbank. The speech touches on research relevant to monetary policy but does not express any monetary policy stance or forward guidance.
rating.stance_rationale: This is a ceremonial/academic laudatory speech with no monetary policy content, rate signals, or policy bias expressed. It is not a monetary policy statement.
key_quotes: The Alexander von Humboldt Professorship: what an extraordinary and well-deserved recognition of Michael's academic achievements.
So, as a central banker I have to admit without envy that, under certain circumstances, such fiscal policy measures can be very effective in stimulating consumption.
